comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
RCA (runtime-proven). Reproduced the no-op churn in isolation: a two-pass runtime probe recorded the SAME authoritative link (LOC-1|LOC-2|blocks, identical link_id/direction/source) across two passes; the on-disk sidecar hash differed between passes (7d849e3… vs 58fba08…) solely because 'confirmed_at' (time.time_ns) and 'confirmed_pass' refreshed. Mechanism: PeerConfirmationStore.record() rebuilds the record every call and sets _dirty=True UNCONDITIONALLY (peer_confirmations.py:142-173); save() then rewrites the full JSON sidecar whenever _dirty (:175-189). Nothing gates the write on a MATERIAL change.

Authority / defect class: this is the 'no-op bridge-state churn' class epic 0303 already governs. peer_state.py codifies 0303's discipline explicitly — bridge-state fields must be 'fixed size, change-gated, never a per-pass timestamp' (peer_state.py rich-emit section; note_rich_emit is change-gated in both directions and a no-op pass writes zero entries). confirmed_at/confirmed_pass are exactly the per-pass timestamps that discipline forbids, so this is a defect, not a design gap.

Consumer contract: repository-wide search finds NO production reader of confirmed_pass or confirmed_at outside the writer; only unit tests assert them (test_peer_confirmations_store.py:162,398; _backfill.py:75; _snapshot.py:91,218-219). is_confirmed()/get() — the safety-critical readers — key only on record EXISTENCE and first_confirmed_at, never on the volatile pair. So the pair is removable telemetry, not a supported audit contract.

Defect origin: the per-pass-timestamp record shape was introduced by nonlineal-melancholy-grouper (248f-ac00-18db-4259, 'Persist a peer-confirmation record per managed link'); it is amplified to every-pass churn by soured-elmy-ostrich (83d3-61d9-fc59-424b, 'Confirm links from authoritative fetched snapshots'), which re-record()s every observed link each pass. caused_by = 248f-ac00-18db-4259.

Fix direction (matches the ticket plan + 0303): remove the volatile confirmed_pass/confirmed_at fields (deliberate removal — no production consumer) and make record() change-gated so an unchanged link leaves _dirty false and save() writes nothing. Keep first_confirmed_at (set-once durable provenance) and all identity/decision fields, preserving relation-scoped, monotonic, additive, fail-open confirmation. One-time bounded migration: the first time each pre-existing record is re-observed post-upgrade its stored shape is rewritten once (dropping the two keys), after which unchanged passes converge to zero writes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Fix landed in worktree + before/after churn evidence (AC5).

Change: PeerConfirmationStore.record() is now change-gated (builds a candidate record from material fields + set-once first_confirmed_at; returns without touching _records or _dirty when it equals the stored record), and the volatile per-pass confirmed_pass / confirmed_at fields are removed. The now-vestigial pass_id parameter is dropped from record(), confirm_from_snapshot(), backfill_from_managed_refs() and their two call sites (reconcile._confirm_peer_links, apply_handlers._make_link_confirm). first_confirmed_at and all identity/decision fields are retained, so confirmation stays relation-scoped, monotonic, additive and fail-open.

Before/after evidence — isolated two-pass runtime probe over ONE unchanged authoritative link (identical inputs, wall clock advanced between passes), hashing the on-disk sidecar each pass:
  BEFORE fix: pass1=7d849e3…, pass2=58fba08… -> DISTINCT -> 2 unique blobs, a full 2nd-file rewrite for zero material change.
  AFTER fix:  pass1=e353435…, pass2=e353435… -> IDENTICAL -> 1 blob, zero new packed bytes on the unchanged pass.
So a converged pass now writes the sidecar zero times (save() early-returns on not-dirty), eliminating the per-pass blob/pack growth this bug reported.

Migration/compat: one-time and bounded. The first time each pre-existing on-disk record is re-observed post-upgrade, its stored shape is rewritten once (dropping confirmed_pass/confirmed_at); after every live link has been observed once, unchanged passes converge to zero writes. The sidecar is fail-open, so a mixed-shape file mid-migration is read without error. No production consumer read the removed fields (repo-wide search; only tests asserted them), so nothing downstream breaks.

Regression tests (RED before fix, GREEN after): test_two_passes_over_unchanged_snapshot_do_not_rewrite_the_sidecar (byte-compares the artifact across two complete persistence passes — AC4), test_reconfirming_unchanged_link_leaves_the_store_not_dirty, and test_reconfirmation_is_idempotent_and_does_not_rewrite. Existing store/backfill/snapshot suites updated to the new contract; assert the volatile fields are absent. make lint + make typecheck + full tests/unit/rebar_reconciler suite green.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / problem

A fresh single-branch clone of the tickets store shows recurring `.bridge_state/peer_confirmations.json` churn even when the authoritative peer link set is unchanged. The current file contains 3,499 records and is 1,400,452 bytes. Git history contains 418 commits touching it and 417 unique blobs totaling 320,864,708 raw bytes. Since the tickets-history rewrite, this path alone contributes 51,853,550 packed-entry bytes.

The latest observed reconcile pass changed 1,225 existing records solely in `confirmed_pass` and `confirmed_at`; no confirmation identity or decision input changed. `PeerConfirmationStore.record()` overwrites those fields and unconditionally sets `_dirty=True` (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/peer_confirmations.py:142-173`), and `save()` then rewrites the full JSON sidecar (`:175-189`). Repository-wide search finds no production reader of either volatile field outside this writer; only tests assert them. A two-pass isolated runtime probe over the same authoritative snapshot wrote the file twice and produced different hashes solely because the pass/time fields refreshed.

This is separate from the principal checkout-size incident: it materially grows reachable Git history, but it does not explain the >1 GB working tree. It recreates the same no-op bridge-state churn class previously addressed for other binding fields.

## Origins / design constraints

The evidence store was introduced by `nonlineal-melancholy-grouper` (`248f-ac00-18db-4259`) and snapshot reconfirmation by `soured-elmy-ostrich` (`83d3-61d9-fc59-424b`). The safety invariant must remain: an observed link is durable positive evidence and absence never un-confirms it. Any repair must decide explicitly whether last-seen pass/time are a supported audit contract or removable telemetry; silently weakening confirmation safety is out of scope.

## Plan

- Establish the intended consumer contract for `confirmed_pass` and `confirmed_at`.
- Add a RED two-pass oracle over an unchanged authoritative snapshot that proves the chosen no-op persistence behavior while preserving confirmation safety and provenance.
- Make persistence content-aware or redesign the volatile telemetry so unchanged link evidence does not rewrite the full sidecar each pass.
- Measure resulting blob/pack churn and document any migration or compatibility implications.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Two identical authoritative snapshots do not create a second full-file content change solely because pass/time advanced, or the approved alternative demonstrably bounds equivalent Git growth. (Change-gated record(); runtime probe two-pass sidecar hash now identical e353435==e353435 vs pre-fix 7d849e3!=58fba08. Regression test test_two_passes_over_unchanged_snapshot_do_not_rewrite_the_sidecar.)
- [x] Link confirmation remains relation-scoped, monotonic, durable across compaction, and fail-open exactly as documented. (Only volatile telemetry removed; keys, is_confirmed(), snapshot/backfill monotonicity, compaction-survival and fail-open paths unchanged; full peer_confirmations + inbound-removal suites green.)
- [x] The supported contract for last-confirmed pass/time is explicit and has a production consumer or is removed/migrated deliberately. (No production reader existed — repo-wide search, only tests asserted them — so confirmed_pass/confirmed_at are removed deliberately; first_confirmed_at retained. One-time bounded per-record migration documented in ticket comment.)
- [x] A regression test exercises two complete persistence passes and compares the on-disk artifact. (test_two_passes_over_unchanged_snapshot_do_not_rewrite_the_sidecar byte-compares the artifact; plus test_reconfirming_unchanged_link_leaves_the_store_not_dirty. RED before fix, GREEN after.)
- [x] Before/after evidence reports unique blob and packed-byte growth for a representative unchanged pass. (See ticket comment: before=2 distinct blobs/full 2nd rewrite per unchanged pass; after=1 blob, zero new packed bytes. Historical path measurement in prior comment: 417 blobs / 6,077,416 objectsize:disk bytes.)
